expectations.text: The reply begins with a progress marker identifying Phase 1.
expectations.evidence: "**Phase 1 of 5 · Explore and choose a direction**"

expectations.text: The reply includes a briefing with four labeled sections covering key debates, major voices, patterns, and open questions.
expectations.evidence: The four required sections are there (Key debates, Major voices, Patterns, Open questions), but there is also a fifth: "**Side effects researchers have found**". Read literally, the briefing has five sections, not four.

expectations.text: The briefing is roughly 300 to 500 words long (it fails if under 250 or over 600 words).
expectations.evidence: From "Key debates" through "Open questions" the briefing comes to roughly 430 words, which is inside the 300–500 range.

expectations.text: The reply presents a mind map, either as an HTML page built from the skill's mind map template or as an indented text tree.
expectations.evidence: "I saved it at .../mind-map.html. Open it in your browser." The assistant read templates/mind-map.html and filled in __MIND_MAP_DATA__.

expectations.text: The mind map has 4 to 6 top-level angles, each with 2 or 3 narrower angles, and every angle has a saturation value between 0 and 1 (or, for a text tree, a crowdedness label).
expectations.evidence: The reply says "It has six angles." Each visible branch has 2–3 children and every angle has a saturation between 0 and 1 (e.g. "saturation": 0.8, 0.5, 0.55, 0.3). The file excerpt is cut off at branch 5, so branch 6 could not be checked.

expectations.text: No mind map label is phrased as a research question; labels are short topics.
expectations.evidence: The labels are short topics, e.g. "Budgets and promised savings" and "Mothers' employment". None is phrased as a question.

expectations.text: The reply does not tell the user which angle they should choose or which one is best.
expectations.evidence: The reply only asks "which direction pulls you most, and why?" and never recommends an angle.

expectations.text: Every link or DOI that appears in the reply or the mind map points to a page the transcript shows Claude opened (fetched) during this session.
expectations.evidence: Every link in the reply and in the visible part of the map was fetched in this session: educationnext, edweek 2026/04, edweek 2024/10, rand RRA373-1.html, idahoednews, edworkingpapers ai21-416, chalkbeat, and the IPUMS entry.

expectations.text: The reply asks the user which direction interests them and why.
expectations.evidence: "After you've explored the map, which direction pulls you most, and why?"

expectations.text: The reply asks the user no more than two questions.
expectations.evidence: The reply asks the user one question. "Feel free to ask me how I know it" is an offer, not a question.
